summary.short: SEC final rule requiring public companies subject to Exchange Act reporting to file a Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days of determining a cybersecurity incident is material, and to describe cybersecurity risk management, strategy and governance in annual reports. Effective September 5, 2023.
summary.long: Adopted by the SEC (Release Nos. 33-11216; 34-97989), this rule amends Regulation S-K, Regulation S-T, and Securities Act and Exchange Act forms and rules for public companies subject to Exchange Act reporting. It adds Form 8-K Item 1.05, requiring disclosure of the material aspects of the nature, scope and timing of a material cybersecurity incident and its material or reasonably likely material impact, within four business days of the materiality determination; information not determined or unavailable at filing may be added by Form 8-K amendment. The Attorney General may, by written notice to the Commission, delay disclosure that poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety, for up to 30 days, extendable by a further 30 days and, in extraordinary circumstances, a final 60 days. Item 106 of Regulation S-K requires annual-report descriptions of processes for assessing, identifying and managing material cybersecurity risks, whether risks have materially affected the registrant, and board and management oversight of those risks. Foreign private issuers furnish incident information on Form 6-K and report under Form 20-F. An untimely Item 1.05 filing does not cause loss of Form S-3 eligibility, and Item 1.05 is added to the safe-harbor list in Rules 13a-11(c) and 15d-11(c). Cybersecurity disclosures are to be presented in Inline XBRL. Asset-backed issuers are exempted from the new rules.

notes: Part 1 of 3 only (front matter, Sections I and II.A–II.D.1 in part). The Statutory Authority section, compliance dates, Item 407(j) text and regulatory text are in later parts, so no legal_basis relation is coded here. Relations to the Proposing Release (Release No. 33–11038), the Reopening Release and CIRCIA regulations are referenced but not coded as target instruments. Footnote 2 cites 15 U.S.C. 78a et seq. for the Exchange Act; this is a citation, not a stated enabling clause in this part. Part 2 of 3 covers Sections I.E to I.I, II.E to II.H, III, IV, V, VI and the start of the amending text (§ 229.106 and the § 229.601 amendment). Preamble material is context; operative Item 1.05 text is in other parts. Inconsistency: Section IV.C.2 says smaller reporting companies are delayed 270 days from effectiveness, yet the stated compliance date is June 15, 2024; by annotator count 270 days from September 5, 2023 is June 1, 2024, while June 15, 2024 is 180 days after December 18, 2023. Relations and entities sections are populated; their section_status entries are set only because the schema requires them. Part 3 of 3 covers § 229.601, the Regulation S-T, S-K, Exchange Act and Securities Act rule amendments, and Forms 6-K, 8-K, 10-K, 20-F (Items 1.05, 1C, 16K). Internal inconsistency: the lists of Form 8-K items excluded from the S-3 eligibility and deemed-violation carve-outs differ across § 239.13(a)(3)(ii), Form S-3 General Instruction I.A.3(b) (which includes Item 1.04 and 5.02(e)) and § 240.13a-11(c) (which includes 5.02(e) and 6.03). Both codes are recorded as written.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment found in this part. The 30-, 60- and seven-business-day delay periods in Form 8-K Item 1.05(c)-(d) and the four-business-day filing rule are procedural time limits (events), not thresholds. The Form S-3 General Instruction I.A.3(b) amendment adds Item 1.05 to the exclusion list and states no number. The Form S-3 twelve-calendar-month lookback is not changed by this part.

enforcement.note: This part sets no sanction regime. Amended §240.13a-11(c) and §240.15d-11(c) state that failing to file a Form 8-K report required solely under listed items (including Item 1.05) 'shall not be deemed a violation' of 15 U.S.C. 78j(b) and §240.10b-5; this is a limit on liability, not a penalty. Item 1.05(c)-(d) provide disclosure delays, not sanctions. Penalty provisions are not reproduced in this part.
